nodes.label: setup_logging (queue-based logging)
nodes.rationale: All processes push records onto a manager Queue consumed by a single QueueListener in the main process, so multiple processes never interleave writes on one stream handler. The root logger's own handlers are cleared with force=True so nothing bypasses the queue.

nodes.label: reopen_std_streams fork hook
nodes.rationale: Registered via os.register_at_fork(after_in_child) to work around CPython issue 91776: if a process is forked while a logging thread holds an internal stdio lock, the child inherits the held lock and deadlocks when Python flushes stdout/stderr at exit. Reopening fds 1 and 2 in the child gives it fresh, unlocked stream objects.

nodes.label: LogPipe (subprocess stderr capture)
nodes.rationale: Buffers the last 100 lines in a bounded deque and only emits them on dump(), so a noisy ffmpeg process does not flood the log until something actually fails. Every line passes through clean_camera_user_pass so RTSP credentials never reach the log.

nodes.label: suppress_stderr_during
nodes.rationale: Native libraries (LLVM, CUDA, TFLite) write straight to file descriptor 2 and ignore Python logging config entirely, so the only way to silence them is to dup2 /dev/null over fd 2 for the duration of the call and restore it afterward.
